question: Estimate the number of distinct job postings published in the United States during calendar year 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) for new-graduate roles — summer internships plus full-time entry-level positions for new bachelor's or master's graduates with 0–1 years of experience, in professional (white-collar) occupations — whose posting text explicitly states that the employer will sponsor a work visa (for example "H-1B sponsorship available" or "visa sponsorship provided"). Count each posting once even if it appears on several job boards. Do not count postings that do not state sponsorship in their text, even if the employer has sponsored visas before or ticks a "will sponsor" box on a job platform, and do not count postings that rule sponsorship out.

target.what: Distinct unique job postings published in the United States during calendar year 2026 for new-graduate roles (summer internships plus full-time entry-level positions for new bachelor's or master's graduates with 0–1 years of experience) in professional white-collar occupations, whose posting text ex
target.publisher: No official publisher; constructed estimate from job-board, employer, and administrative evidence
target.cadence: Annual flow; no single reporting series exists
target.caveats: The target period is ongoing relative to the 2026-10-28 cutoff, so 2026 Q4 must be projected. Working interpretation: count unique requisitions/postings, not applications, hires, or job-board listings; deduplicate across boards. Alternative interpretations that would materially change the answer: (a

candidates.perspective: Job-board and labor-market data providers (Lightcast, Indeed Hiring Lab, LinkUp, Revelio, Handshake)
candidates.hypothesis: Total US new-graduate professional postings in 2026 multiplied by the share whose text explicitly mentions visa sponsorship yields the target. The share is the key bridge; total postings volume is the broader total.
candidates.data_to_find: Annual or monthly counts of US postings for entry-level/new-graduate professional roles in 2025 and 2026 YTD from Lightcast, Indeed Hiring Lab, LinkUp, or Handshake; plus any reported share or count of postings mentioning 'visa sponsorship', 'H-1B', or 'sponsorship available'. Minimum evidence: a total postings count for the relevant occupation/experience filter and at least one sponsorship-mention share estimate.
search_hints: Lightcast job postings data 2026 entry level
share of job postings mentioning visa sponsorship
Handshake new graduate job postings report

candidates.perspective: Sponsorship-focused job boards and trackers (MyVisaJobs, H1BGrader, Interstride, Simplify, sponsor-friendly job lists)
candidates.hypothesis: Sponsorship-filtered job boards publish counts of open roles tagged as offering sponsorship; their annual flow of unique postings, adjusted for coverage and deduplication, approximates the target. These boards over-represent sponsorship-stating employers but under-cover the full market.
candidates.data_to_find: Annual counts of sponsorship-tagged postings on MyVisaJobs, H1BGrader, Interstride, or similar, for 2024–2026, with scope (occupations, experience levels, geography) and whether counts are listings or unique requisitions. Minimum evidence: one platform's annual posting count plus a coverage/deduplication adjustment factor.

candidates.hypothesis: H-1B registrations, LCA filings, and OPT/STEM-OPT approvals bound the number of sponsoring employers and sponsored roles; the ratio of sponsorship-stating postings to eventual LCA/registration filings provides a scaling factor. Administrative counts are a floor/constraint, not the target itself.
candidates.data_to_find: FY2025–FY2026 H-1B registration and selection counts, LCA filings by employer and occupation, and OPT/STEM-OPT approval counts for new graduates. Minimum evidence: annual LCA or registration totals and an estimate of postings per sponsored hire.
search_hints: DOL LCA disclosure data FY2025 filings

candidates.perspective: Employer career sites and ATS data (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever) for large sponsoring employers
candidates.hypothesis: Top H-1B-sponsoring employers (tech, consulting, finance, engineering) post a measurable number of new-graduate roles; summing across the top N sponsors and scaling to the full sponsor population gives the target. Sponsorship-stating language is concentrated among known sponsors.
candidates.data_to_find: Counts of 2026 new-graduate postings at the top 50–200 H-1B-sponsoring employers, and the share of those postings that explicitly state sponsorship. Minimum evidence: posting counts for a sample of large sponsors plus a sponsorship-statement share within that sample.
search_hints: Workday careers sponsorship available entry level

candidates.perspective: Historical sponsorship-stating posting volumes and seasonality
candidates.hypothesis: The target's prior-year values and within-year seasonality (internship recruiting peaks in fall/winter, full-time entry-level peaks in spring) can extrapolate 2026 YTD to a full year. If no direct series exists, use prior-year sponsorship-tagged posting counts from boards as a proxy history.
candidates.data_to_find: 2023–2025 annual or monthly counts of sponsorship-stating new-graduate postings from any consistent source, plus 2026 monthly counts through October. Minimum evidence: a monthly series for at least one prior year and 2026 YTD to estimate the Q4 share.
search_hints: visa sponsorship job postings monthly trend
new grad hiring seasonality internship postings

candidates.perspective: University career services and new-graduate labor market
candidates.hypothesis: The number of new bachelor's/master's graduates entering the professional labor market, multiplied by the share of postings/roles that state sponsorship and the application-to-posting ratio, constrains the target. Graduate supply and employer demand for sponsored candidates bound the count.
candidates.data_to_find: Annual US bachelor's and master's graduates in professional fields (NCES/IPEDS), international student counts (SEVIS), and employer demand indicators for sponsored new graduates. Minimum evidence: graduate counts by field and an estimate of sponsored-role share of entry-level demand.
search_hints: NCES bachelor's degrees conferred 2025 by field

candidates.hypothesis: Changes in H-1B policy (fee increases, registration rules, wage-based selection), immigration enforcement, and tech-sector hiring affect both the number of sponsorship-stating postings and employer willingness to state sponsorship. Direction and magnitude of 2026 deviation from historical trend must be assessed.
candidates.data_to_find: 2025–2026 H-1B policy changes (fees, selection rules), tech/consulting hiring trends, and any reported shifts in employer sponsorship language. Minimum evidence: documented policy changes with effective dates and any measured effect on posting volumes or sponsorship mentions.
search_hints: employers removing visa sponsorship job postings

candidates.perspective: Job seekers and media tracking sponsorship-friendly roles
candidates.hypothesis: Search interest and media coverage of 'sponsorship jobs' correlate with the volume of sponsorship-stating postings; attention data can validate trend direction but requires a bridge to posting counts.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends or job-board search volume for 'visa sponsorship jobs' and 'H-1B jobs' 2023–2026, plus any media-reported counts of sponsorship-friendly postings. Minimum evidence: a consistent attention series and at least one anchor linking attention to posting volume.

methods.rationale: Volume-times-share decomposition: total 2026 new-grad professional postings times the Handshake 2026 sponsorship share, adjusted for definitional gaps. The share is the only direct early-career sponsorship measurement; the volume is an assumption because no kept point counts total postings. Failure modes: Handshake's 2.6% may be a platform flag rather than explicit text, and the volume assumption is very wide.

methods.rationale: Administrative route: FY2025 initial-employment approvals (114,806) times postings-per-approval times a 2026 policy change factor. This anchors the level on an administrative count rather than a survey share, but the two coefficients are assumptions; the fee shock (p138) is the dominant uncertainty. methods.rationale: Employer-count route: 28,277 sponsoring employers times postings-per-approval (used as a per-employer scale proxy) times the 2026 change factor. This is a weaker variant of m2 because approvals-per-employer varies enormously (p58-p60), so it is retained only as a cross-check on the administrative scale; it shares inputs a4 and a5 with m2 and is not independent.

assumptions.name: Total US new-grad professional postings in 2026
assumptions.rationale: No kept point gives the total volume of US new-grad/internship professional postings. Anchored on the scale implied by ~2.0M bachelor's degrees plus ~0.8M master's degrees conferred annually (p170, p171) and the fact that each graduate applies to many postings; set well below graduate counts times a large application ratio because many postings are non-professional or filled internally. Wide range reflects the absence of a direct count.
assumptions.applies_when: Used only as the denominator volume that the Handshake sponsorship share (p224) is applied to; if a direct posting-volume count is found, replace it.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published count of US early-career postings (Handshake, Indeed, Lightcast) outside the 0.5M-3M range.

assumptions.name: Adjustment of 2026 Handshake sponsorship share to the target's explicit-text definition
assumptions.rationale: Handshake's 2.6% (p224) is measured on full-time postings and may include platform 'will sponsor' flags rather than explicit posting text; the target requires explicit text and also includes internships. The two definitional gaps could push either way, so the factor is centred at 1 with a factor-of-two range.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the Handshake 2026 share when converting it to the target's explicit-text, internship-inclusive definition.
assumptions.falsified_by: Documentation showing Handshake's 2.6% is text-based and covers internships, or that it is purely a checkbox flag (which would require a downward factor).

assumptions.name: Share of 2026 new-grad professional postings that are internships
assumptions.rationale: The target sums internships and full-time entry-level roles; NACE reports intern hiring growing ~4% (p159, p186) while full-time new-grad hiring grows ~5.6% (p162), and employers recruit for both (p191). Internships are typically a minority of early-career postings because most entry-level hiring is full-time; 25% with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to check that the internship component is not double-counted or omitted when applying a full-time-based share.
assumptions.falsified_by: A board count showing internships are a majority or a negligible share of early-career postings.

assumptions.name: Ratio of sponsorship-stating postings to new H-1B initial-employment approvals
assumptions.rationale: Employers post many requisitions per eventual sponsored hire (screening, multiple openings, interns who later convert). With 114,806 FY2025 initial approvals (p56) and 28,277 employers (p57), a ratio of a few postings per approval is plausible; the range spans one-to-one up to a tenfold funnel.
assumptions.applies_when: Used in the administrative route that scales FY2025 approvals to 2026 sponsorship-stating postings, after applying the 2026 policy change factor.
assumptions.falsified_by: Employer-level data showing postings-per-sponsored-hire is far outside 1-10.

assumptions.name: 2026 change factor in sponsorship-stating postings vs FY2025 baseline
assumptions.rationale: The $100,000 new-petition fee (p138, p142) and reported employer pauses (p143, p144) plus the 27% drop in FY2026 registrations (p47, p90) point to a decline in stated sponsorship; Handshake's share fell from ~11% (2023) to 2.6% (2026) (p223, p224). A factor below 1 with a wide range reflects uncertainty about how much of the decline is already in the FY2025 baseline.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the FY2025 approval-based posting estimate to move it to calendar 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that sponsorship-stating postings rose or were flat in 2026 despite the fee.

kept.name: Adjustment of 2026 Handshake sponsorship share to the target's explicit-text, internship-inclusive definition
kept.rationale: The Handshake 2.6% (p224) is measured on full-time postings; the target also includes internships, which are less likely to state sponsorship, and requires explicit text, which the Handshake tag may not exactly match. A factor centered at 1 with a factor-of-two range covers both directions.
kept.applies_when: The Handshake share is used as the sponsorship-stating share of early-career postings.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Handshake's tag counts platform checkboxes rather than posting text, or that internship sponsorship-stating rates differ by more than 2x from full-time.

kept.name: Total US new-grad professional postings in 2026 as a multiple of annual bachelor's degree conferrals
kept.rationale: No kept point gives the total volume of new-grad professional postings. Anchoring on ~2.0M bachelor's degrees/year (p170) and the fact that each graduate applies to many postings but many postings are filled by non-new-grads or through networks, a ratio of 0.6 postings per degree (range 0.25-1.5) sp
kept.applies_when: The target is interpreted as unique requisitions for 0-1 year professional roles, internships plus entry-level, and degree conferrals proxy the new-grad cohort.
kept.falsified_by: A published count of US new-grad postings (e.g. Handshake or Lightcast annual total) implying a ratio outside 0.25-1.5.

kept.name: Ratio of sponsorship-stating postings to new H-1B initial-employment approvals
kept.rationale: Each new H-1B initial-employment approval corresponds to at least one sponsorship-stating requisition, but employers post many roles per sponsored hire. A ratio of 3 (range 1-10) reflects that most sponsorship-stating postings do not result in a petition.
kept.applies_when: Sponsorship-stating postings scale with new H-1B initial-employment approvals.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that sponsorship-stating postings per approval are below 1 or above 10.

kept.name: 2026 change factor in sponsorship-stating postings vs FY2025 baseline
kept.rationale: The $100,000 new H-1B fee (p138) and employer pauses (p143, p144) point to a decline in sponsorship-stating postings in 2026, while Handshake's 2.6% share (p224) already reflects the drop from 10.9% in 2023. A factor of 0.6 (range 0.25-1.2) captures a substantial but not catastrophic decline.
kept.applies_when: FY2025 H-1B approval counts are used as a baseline for calendar 2026 sponsorship-stating postings.
kept.falsified_by: A board's before/after count showing sponsorship-stating postings flat or up in 2026.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
